title: Write-Ahead Log
description: Understand write-ahead logging for crash recovery, checkpointing strategies, and the ARIES recovery algorithm.

segments.text: Databases promise durability. Your committed transaction must survive a power failure. But writing to disk after every transaction is slow. The Write-Ahead Log, or WAL, is how databases square this circle.

The rule is simple: before modifying any data page on disk, first write a log record describing the change to a sequential log file. Sequential writes are fast. Random writes to data pages can happen later, lazily.

Each log record contains: a log sequence number, the transaction ID, the page being modified, the before-image of the data, and the after-image. The before-image supports undo, the after-image supports redo.

The system crashes. Some transactions committed but their data pages never reached disk. Some transactions were in progress and partially wrote data. We need to redo the first group and undo the second.

segments.thought_prompt: If the log has millions of records, do you replay from the very beginning every time? That could take hours.

segments.text: That is where checkpointing comes in. Periodically, the database flushes all dirty pages to disk and writes a checkpoint record to the log. During recovery, you only need to replay from the last checkpoint forward.

A full checkpoint stalls the database while flushing. Fuzzy checkpoints are better: record which pages are dirty and which transactions are active, then flush pages in the background. No stall required.

ARIES is the gold standard recovery algorithm, used by PostgreSQL, DB2, and SQL Server. It has three phases: Analysis scans the log to determine the state at crash time. Redo replays all changes. Undo reverses uncommitted transactions.

Analysis phase: scan from the last checkpoint. Rebuild the dirty page table to know which pages need redo. Rebuild the active transaction table to know which transactions need undo. This gives recovery its starting point.

Redo phase: replay log records forward from the earliest dirty page LSN. This restores the exact database state at crash time. Undo phase: walk backward through the log, undoing changes from uncommitted transactions.

segments.thought_prompt: What if the system crashes DURING recovery? Does ARIES handle a crash during the undo phase?

segments.text: Yes. ARIES writes compensation log records during undo, so if recovery itself crashes, the next recovery can skip already-undone work. This is idempotent recovery. WAL and ARIES are why your bank transactions survive power outages. Elegant, battle-tested, and fundamental.
